nodes.label: AI-Powered Recruitment Platform Overview
nodes.rationale: Combines traditional recruitment workflow management with resume parsing, semantic job-resume matching, embeddings, LLM analysis, RAG, scoring, ranking, assessments, coding evaluation and interview analysis in one platform.

nodes.label: User Roles (PLATFORM_ADMIN, ADMIN, RECRUITER)
nodes.rationale: PLATFORM_ADMIN verifies companies at platform level and is only partially implemented; ADMIN and RECRUITER both belong to exactly one company. ADMIN sees company-wide data, RECRUITER only its permitted recruitment data, so role alone determines authorization scope.

nodes.label: Company Isolation Security Requirement
nodes.rationale: Declared the critical security requirement: every User and Job belongs to a Company, a recruiter must never reach another company's data, ownership is always enforced by the backend, and companyId from the frontend is never trusted.

nodes.label: End-to-End Recruitment Workflow
nodes.rationale: Company registration and verification, then admin creates recruiters, recruiter creates jobs and uploads resumes, then parse, embed, compare, score, explain, rank, shortlist, assess, interview and AI interview analysis to final evaluation.

nodes.label: AI Resume Screening Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Text extraction, normalization, embedding generation and vector storage on the resume side are compared to the job embedding by semantic similarity to produce a matching score, with an LLM explanation layered on top so the score is defensible, not opaque.

nodes.label: Python AI Service Boundary
nodes.rationale: AI lives in Python and communicates over HTTP REST returning JSON, but Java Spring Boot explicitly remains the main backend: 'Do not move the entire application to Python.' This keeps auth, tenancy and relational data in one trusted service.

nodes.label: JWT Claim Policy
nodes.rationale: Only sub, userId, role, companyId, iat and exp are allowed; password, password hash, phone number, company detail, candidate and resume information are excluded because a JWT identifies the user but does not authorize anything on its own - database queries and backend checks enforce actual ownership.

nodes.label: CustomUserDetails SecurityContext Chain
nodes.rationale: CustomUserDetails wraps the User entity so the current company is reachable as customUserDetails.getUser().getCompany().getId(); this is the designated substitute for accepting companyId from a client request.

nodes.label: Company Verification Flow (planned)
nodes.rationale: Admin email verification, email link, phone OTP, submitted verification details, then Platform Admin review before companyVerified=true. The frontend must never set companyVerified, so trust is only ever granted by the platform side.

nodes.label: Company Identity & Uniqueness Criteria
nodes.rationale: Registration number is the intended duplicate-company identity criterion, with GST number optionally unique; company email and phone are deliberately NOT identity criteria because multiple legitimate companies can share or change contact details.
